rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Sustainability keeps harvest and waste inside what the system can renew and absorb. Forests, water and soil are renewable only within a rate. Coal and oil are not renewed on a human timescale. Using less, reusing and recycling, as in a well-run community forest, is the practical test.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
A sustainable use takes no more of a resource, and dumps no more waste, than the system can replace or absorb.
Climate pressure, polluted air and water, loss of habitat and the using-up of freshwater and fertile soil are the four pressures named in this note.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Renewable does not mean infinite. A forest can be overcut.  ·  Recycling is not a licence to waste more.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The Paris Agreement (2015) sets targets to limit global warming to well below 2°C.  ·  Biodiversity hotspots (e.g., Amazon rainforest, coral reefs) are critical for ecosystem resilience.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Renewable resources renew if the harvest stays below the renewal. A forest cut faster than it grows is being used as if it were a mine.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Stay inside this class 11 topic.  ·  Do not add an unsupported count.

rows.text: Climate change = greenhouse gases + global warming.  ·  Sustainability = economic + social + environmental balance.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Connect environmental science with policy (e.g., carbon taxes, renewable energy mandates).  ·  Understand the difference between renewable and non-renewable resources.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Carbon cycle: exchange of carbon between atmosphere, oceans, and living organisms  ·  Water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, runoff  ·  Ecosystem services: provisioning, regulating, cultural, and supporting services  ·  Sustainable development: meeting present needs without compromising future generations

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere, causing global warming.  ·  Deforestation reduces carbon sequestration capacity and disrupts water cycles.  ·  Circular economy principles aim to minimize waste and maximize resource reuse.  ·  Use no faster than renewal.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: How does deforestation affect the carbon cycle?  ·  Explain the concept of ecosystem services.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Consider the socio-economic dimensions of sustainability (equity, justice).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Non-renewable resources, such as coal and oil, are not replaced on a human timescale. Sustainability then means using less and wasting less.  ·  Reduce, reuse and recycle cut the demand and the rubbish. Community forestry in Nepal is a worked case of a renewable resource brought back under local rules.  ·  A practice fails the test if it solves today's need by destroying the stock the next harvest depends on. That is the whole standard.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Forest, water, soil, fuel.  ·  Reduce, reuse, recycle.  ·  Community forestry as a case.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Community forestry is management, not a new species.  ·  Pollution is a waste problem, not a separate planet from resource use.  ·  Sustainable agriculture practices (crop rotation, cover cropping) reduce environmental impact.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Order in a sequence is part of the answer.  ·  Do not call a timberline a snowline.  ·  Climate change is driven primarily by greenhouse gas emissions (CO2, methane, nitrous oxide).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Sustainability requires balancing economic growth, social equity, and environmental protection.  ·  Renewable energy sources (solar, wind, hydro) reduce reliance on fossil fuels.  ·  Ecosystem services = benefits humans derive from nature.
